India has one of the world's largest bodies of rock art, from the painted shelters of Bhimbetka to the engravings of the Konkan coast. The lecture looks at what the images depict, how they are dated, and how researchers document them before they fade.

Length, level and language are agreed with you. The lecture can be given online or at your venue, for a single class, a department or a whole organisation.

What it covers

  • The painted shelters of Bhimbetka and central India
  • The rock engravings of the Konkan coast
  • How rock art is dated
  • How it is recorded and protected

How the time is spent

  1. Where and when 20 min

    Rock shelters and regional variability.

    You: map sites

  2. Documentation 35 min

    Motifs, pigment, superimposition and dating limits.

    You: image tracing

  3. Interpretation 20 min

    Avoid treating motifs as self-explanatory.

    You: evidence response

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Describe the painted shelters of Bhimbetka and the rock engravings of the Konkan coast.
  • Explain how rock art is dated and why dating it has limits.
  • Describe how rock art is documented through motifs, pigment and superimposition.
